sections.heading: C — Alcohol, Drugs and Driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol, Drugs and Driving

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Mind-altering drugs plus many prescriptions and over-the-counter cold, allergy, pain, and diet pills all bend perception and reaction, slow responses, dizzy, unnerve, and blur concentration and vision, strike each body and each occasion differently with weight, mood, heart and breath, food, sleep, and tolerance all shifting the blow, and even small doses dull judgment, decision, and action behind the wheel [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Mixed drugs react together and multiply concentration and coordination harm, worst with alcohol aboard, where multiplied effects plus brand-new reactions can sicken or kill [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Alcohol races from stomach to blood to body with judgment impaired almost at once and good sense suspended past self-knowledge, slows reflexes, reaction, sight, and alertness with worsening judgment and skill as doses climb, warps distance, speed, and motion reading plus vehicle control, claims about one-quarter of highway deaths, maims youth beyond all other causes, and meets toughened Oklahoma laws and enforcement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Alcohol counts by amount not by drink, with a twelve-ounce beer, a five-ounce wine, and a one-and-one-half-ounce eighty-proof cocktail all equal [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A02
Impaired driving between point-oh-five and point-oh-eight blood alcohol convicts to one hundred to five hundred dollars, up to six months in jail, or both, under penalties toughest for drivers under twenty-one with lifelong record consequences [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A02
Driving or holding actual physical control consents every resident and visitor to blood-alcohol testing, refusals revoke privileges automatically even when sober, and point-oh-eight or more or any measurable youth amount revokes licenses even without court conviction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A02
Impairment starts below legal limits, officer observations of behavior, appearance, and mannerisms can convict without any test, driving impaired by any substance stays prohibited, concentrations above point-oh-five evidence impairment, and DUI means intoxication by drugs, alcohol, or both [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Conviction notices suspend privileges thirty days first, six months second, and one year third [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Point-oh-eight-plus DUI convicts to jail AND fines, with first offenses misdemeanors of ten days to one year plus up to one thousand dollars, second offenses within ten years felonies of one to five years plus up to two thousand five hundred dollars, second felonies of one to seven years plus up to five thousand dollars, and third or later offenses of one to ten years plus up to five thousand dollars [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A03
DUI convictions suspend or revoke for one hundred eighty days first, one year with a prior in-ten-years revocation, and two years with two or more, unless the same incident already revoked the privilege by refusal or failure [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A03
Alcohol arrests pile lawyer bills, lost work, substitute rides, court costs, substance-abuse evaluations, ignition interlocks, reinstatement fees, insurance hikes, drunk-driver stigma, and felony fallout on loans, colleges, and scholarships for life [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A03
Non-alcohol drugs can out-impair alcohol with prescription-plus-alcohol mixes turning deadly, drug labels warn of drowsy or nervous driving while diet and pep pills rebound into jitters, dizziness, fog, and warped sight with pharmacists and doctors as referees, marijuana multiplies mistakes, glare trouble, and tickets and stays illegal at any detectable driving level despite medical legalization, and illegal drugs wreck safety with amphetamine drivers four times crash-prone [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A04
Under-twenty-one drivers break the law by any measurable alcohol, any other intoxicating substance, or their combination behind the wheel or in actual control, with zero-tolerance revocations of six months first and twelve months second plus extensions to age sixteen for the youngest [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A04
Youth fines run one hundred to five hundred dollars first and one hundred to one thousand later, each swappable with service, treatment, or blends, while courts must report every under-eighteen alcohol or drug offense for license cancellation or denial of six months, one year, two years, or until twenty-one whichever lasts longest [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0067]
